items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: But I did meet him, actually, at the Warwick Ballroom on 47th Street.

ctx.x: That's when he came back from Fletcher's band?

Yeah, he was playing -- this was 1927. And he was playing at the Plantation. But I did meet him, actually, at the Warwick Ballroom on 47th Street. On Sunday afternoon they was playing a dance there. But now [unintelligible] I had an opportunity to try out for a band which was called the "Society Syncopaters." And before the rehearsal we had a jam session and everybody was so thrilled with me because, you know, I was playing all the Coleman Hawkins stuff, and alto at that time, you know.

So now the leader was happy, he was going to get me a job with the band. So now the rehearsal started. Well then they found out I couldn't read. So the leader was very nice. He said to me, "well, you play very good but you've got to learn how to read." But, he said, I have a man that maybe can help you out. So he gave me the phone number and address of a man, a piano player named Bill Fry.
